clue.text: Have drinking spree with Liberal where "You'll never walk alone" comes from

definitions.text: where "You'll never walk alone" comes from

blocks.note: to carouse is to drink heavily and noisily
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Football fans go on a bender, and someone wonders where their anthem originally came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool fans sing the song, which pulls the mind towards football, but it was written for a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The song first appeared in the 1945 Rodgers and Hammerstein musical of that title, so the show is its source.

clue.text: Following Conservative legislation, support tax maybe

indicators.note: following tells us the legislation comes after the party abbreviation rather than before it

explanation.surface: A Tory government passes a law and then backs a new tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A clawback is money the state recovers, and a tax is one example of such recovery, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Odd, peculiar, non-uniform, copy

indicators.note: uniform is the phonetic-alphabet word for one letter, and non- tells us to remove that letter
odd means strange or irregular, so the remaining letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of adjectives describing something strange and irregular, ending with the claim it is only a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet; drop it from peculiar, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an original, which is a copy.

clue.text: Weapon seizure upset to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the following word is used, so the letters sit inside it
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the letters after the opening se

explanation.surface: A gun confiscation causes some upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Banishment from English team extremely lamentable

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An England side's dismal performance gets them sent away in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is enforced absence from one's homeland, the same thing as banishment.

clue.text: Where leader passed — capital place to sleep, I hesitate to say

blocks.note: a bunk is a bed, especially on a ship or in bunk beds
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A hesitant speaker mentions where a leader died, a place in the capital where one sleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader is Hitler, who died in 1945 in the shelter beneath the Reich Chancellery; the clue only hints at him, hence the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitler died by suicide in his underground shelter in the German capital, so that shelter is where the leader passed away.

clue.text: Untrustworthy person in shelter after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A traitor hides in a refuge once the uprising has happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A slippery customer is called an eel, from the fish that is hard to grasp.

clue.text: Beneficiary seen entering castle gate eagerly

indicators.note: the answer is found going into the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: end of castle, all of gate, start of eagerly

explanation.surface: An heir is spotted rushing through a castle gate to claim the inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is a person who receives a legacy under a will, a beneficiary.

clue.text: Character, grown-up, getting new start

indicators.note: getting a new start means the opening letter is swapped for the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An adult with a strong personality makes a fresh start in life.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their essential temperament, their character.

clue.text: Strengthening device sufficient provided current included? Right

indicators.note: included says the conditional word and the current symbol go inside the word for sufficient

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a gadget is adequate given that current flows through it, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Right' read like a query and its confirmation; Right simply supplies a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier is an electronic device that boosts the strength of a signal.

clue.text: Managed to include company protecting another one producing fur

indicators.note: to include means the word for managed wraps around everything that follows
to protect something is to surround it, so one company encloses the other

blocks.note: ran a business means managed it
another company, the same abbreviation again

explanation.surface: A firm takes on a partner company to make fur products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second company, so the same two letters appear inside themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon is a North American mammal whose pelt was traded as fur, so it is an animal producing fur.

clue.text: Illumination from old BBC radio programme

blocks.note: first meaning: brightness that lets us see
second meaning: the BBC ... Programme, a station replaced by Radio 2 in 1967

explanation.surface: Enlightenment came from an old radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC Light Programme was a British radio station of light entertainment, broadcasting from 1945 to 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both visible brightness and, in BBC history, the name of a popular radio service.

clue.text: Film short meeting

explanation.surface: A short film is screened at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Short film is a familiar phrase, but here Film alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is David Lean's 1945 British romance about a chance meeting at a railway station.

clue.text: Ali, say, in plane

blocks.note: first meaning: Muhammad Ali was a boxer, one example of the type
second meaning: a fast military aircraft built for combat

explanation.surface: Muhammad Ali takes a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer like Ali is a prizefighter, and a combat aircraft is also called by the same word.

clue.text: See 12
Latest reports of cheerful romantic meetings

explanation.surface: News bulletins about happy courtships.
explanation.definitionFit: Updates are the newest pieces of information, the most recent reports.

clue.text: Warhorse once — source of continuing power

blocks.note: first meaning: a knight's horse ridden into battle in former times
second meaning: a device that keeps a battery topped up

explanation.surface: An old cavalry horse still provides energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A steed ridden in a cavalry charge was so called, and a battery recharging device bears the same name.

clue.text: Unexpectedly dire new drink

indicators.note: something unexpected does not follow the usual order, so the letters come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprisingly awful new beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret or merlot is wine made from dark grapes, a common drink.

clue.text: Very many dogs not needing lead

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, and not needing it means dropping it

blocks.note: poodles are a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Plenty of dogs are well trained enough to walk without a leash.
explanation.walkthrough: The lead looks like a dog's leash, but it means the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it means lots, as very many does.

clue.text: Some mishaps — alter your instrument

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: end of mishaps, all of alter, start of your

explanation.surface: After a few accidents, someone is told to change their musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument plucked with the fingers, like a small zither.

clue.text: Global body French article briefly describes

blocks.note: setter's reading: the French indefinite article un is also the short form of this body's name

explanation.surface: A worldwide organisation is described in a French newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: Article means a newspaper piece in the surface but the grammatical word un here, which doubles as the body's two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The organisation of 193 member states founded in 1945 is the principal worldwide intergovernmental institution.

clue.text: Recent arrival's renown at work captivates British

indicators.note: something at work is being processed, so its letters are reworked
to captivate is to hold captive, so the letters enclose another

explanation.surface: A newcomer's fame in the workplace charms the British public.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby just delivered is the most recent arrival in a family.

clue.text: See 20
Kick-off opportunity

blocks.note: first meaning: the start of something
second meaning: a chance, such as a job vacancy

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a beginning and a gap or chance that someone can take.

clue.text: Page about wonderful building?

explanation.surface: A page describing a marvellous piece of architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: not every building is of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a factory-made building assembled on site, common in post-war Britain.

clue.text: Person writing cheque on return home — grand,  providing funds

indicators.note: on return means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the drawer of a cheque is the person who writes it
G stands for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone back home writes a cheque for a thousand to fund a project.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand looks like praise but is slang for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewarding someone means giving them money or recompense, so providing funds to them.

clue.text: Progress in good school

blocks.note: Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: Advancing in life by attending a good school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on in life is to advance or succeed, which is to progress.

clue.text: Period of fascination

blocks.note: first meaning: a stretch of time
second meaning: a charm or enchantment that holds someone

explanation.surface: A time when someone was enthralled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a short stretch of time and a magical charm that captivates.

clue.text: Plants from State I'd overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Someone has missed some plants from a particular state.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plant life of a region.

clue.text: Excellent batches oddly abandoned

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are thrown away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Superb bakery batches were strangely left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace is informal for first-rate, which is excellent.

clue.text: Hand over text I read differently

indicators.note: reading something in another way changes its order, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written; the word does double duty

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a document they have interpreted in another way.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to surrender a suspect to another country's jurisdiction, handing them over.

clue.text: Associate failing to finish everything

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is missing

explanation.surface: A colleague does not complete every task.
explanation.definitionFit: All means the whole quantity, the entirety, which is everything.

clue.text: See 5
Ultimately terrible analogy recollected deadly cargo's bearer

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word
re-collected means gathered up again, so the letters are reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a dreadful comparison involving a lethal shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' looks like remembered but splits as collected again.
explanation.definitionFit: The B-29 bomber of that name dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima in 1945, carrying a lethal payload.
